query: The Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy previously showed limited amorphous retention and a complicated thermal response. Earlier thermal studies of Ni–P and Pd–Ni–P alloys found that rapid quenching could produce amorphous material, but that its stability was limited during subsequent heating. The design challenge is therefore to obtain robust glass formation across relevant cooling conditions without sacrificing stability during reheating. What single intervention could improve amorphous retention and thermal stability during solidification and thermal analysis? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to the reported behavior of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20, the cooling-rate and reheating conditions under which it should or should not succeed, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing 2 at.% of P with B to obtain Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P18B2 will increase the glass-forming ability and elevate the crystallization onset temperature, so that (i) fully amorphous ribbons can be obtained at wheel speeds ⩾20 m s⁻¹ (≈1 × 10⁵ K s⁻¹) where the parent Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy partly crystallises, and (ii) DSC reheating at 20 K min⁻¹ will show the first exotherm shifted ≥40 K higher than for the P-only alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: Arc-melted Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 master ingot (pre-alloyed, fully molten).
generation.intervention: Add 2 at.% B at the expense of P before melt-spinning, giving nominal composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P18B2.
generation.conditions: Rapid solidification by melt-spinning at wheel surface velocities 10–40 m s⁻¹ followed by DSC scans at 20 K min⁻¹ up to 800 K in Ar.
generation.structural_mediator: Random covalent P–B network embedded in the multicomponent metallic matrix, increasing packing density and topological frustration.
generation.mechanism:
1. B has a smaller atomic radius and forms strong negative-ΔH_mix bonds with the 3d elements and P, enhancing chemical short-range order and suppressing atomic diffusion.
2. Added size/enthalpy mismatch raises the liquid’s viscosity, enabling glass formation at lower cooling rates.
3. The P–B covalent network increases the energy barrier for nucleation and growth, delaying crystallisation during reheating, hence raising T_x.
generation.predicted_outcome:
Compared with Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20:
• XRD of ribbons spun at 20 m s⁻¹ will show only broad amorphous humps instead of mixed amorphous+crystalline peaks.
• DSC will reveal the first crystallisation onset (T_x) ≥40 K higher and the ∆H_cr reduced, indicating improved thermal stability.
generation.baseline: Parent Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 requires ≥30 m s⁻¹ (≈3 × 10⁵ K s⁻¹) for mostly amorphous ribbons and shows T_x ≈ 585 K with multiple, closely spaced exotherms.
generation.boundary: Benefit expected for 0.5 ≤ B ≤ 5 at.%; above ~5 at.% B phase separation or boride precipitation may counteract GFA. Cooling rates <10³ K s⁻¹ or heating rates ≪10 K min⁻¹ may still allow crystallisation even with B.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of T_x increase (≈40 K) is estimated from trends in Fe–Ni–(P,B) glasses; actual shift may vary with ribbon thickness and residual stresses.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two melts: (A) Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 (control) and (B) Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P18B2. Produce ribbons at 15, 20, 25, 30 m s⁻¹. Characterise each by XRD, DSC, and TEM.
measurements: Phase fraction amorphous vs crystalline from XRD/Rietveld
Onset temperature of first DSC exotherm (T_x)
TEM selected-area diffraction for local amorphous verification
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If composition B does not (i) raise T_x by ≥20 K nor (ii) increase the amorphous fraction at 20 m s⁻¹ by at least 20 percentage points relative to control, the hypothesis is falsified.
